targets.title: The ventriloquist effect results from near-optimal bimodal integration
targets.evidence_quote:
This study aimed to examine whether the MLE model accurately predicts the results of untrained participants in an audiovisual localization task that was designed to be nearly identical to the study by
Alais and Burr (2004)
.
targets.outcome_quote: In conclusion, naive observers do not integrate audiovisual spatial signals in a way that is consistent with the principles of maximum likelihood estimation. These results may be explained by observers' uncertainty about whether the sensory signals share a common origin, as accounted for by models of Bayesian causal inference.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central claim is MLE consistency. The authors' overall conclusion rejects that claim despite obtaining the predicted variance reduction.

reasoning: Full text identity matches title, DOI and four authors. Completed registered report collecting new data. Alais and Burr is explicitly the nearly identical study being retested. Battaglia et al. motivates the competing prediction and power calculation and is discussed as convergent prior evidence; it is not independently retested as a target.
